music/music-pitch.16aec3e49448: 五声音阶 pentatonic. Five notes: 宫 商 角 徵 羽. 宫 gōng, 商 shāng, 角 jué, 徵 zhǐ, 羽 yǔ equals one, two, three, five, six, do re mi sol la. No half steps, so any combination sounds smooth — it is the base of most Chinese folk music, and also of blues, Scottish and West African tunes.
music/music-pitch.b1eeb28c1089: Don't mix up: 徵 is read zhǐ here, not zhēng, and 角 is jué, not jiǎo.
music/music-pitch.b7e6e45a5b04: Don't mix up: 简谱 numbers are scale degrees, not fixed pitches — one is not always C.
music/music-pitch.7a23e8e651e5: Interval. The distance between two notes. Count letter names, including both ends: C to G equals C D E F G equals a fifth. Small whole-number frequency ratios sound smooth: octave two to one, fifth three to two.
music/music-pitch.93522c381a9f: Staff and clefs. A map for pitch. Higher on the staff equals higher pitch. Treble clef, G clef, curls around G four; bass clef, F clef, has two dots around F three.
music/music-pitch.2d3ec38021f3: Pitch and frequency. How high or low a sound is. Pitch depends on frequency: vibrations per second, measured in hertz, H Z. A four equals four hundred forty hertz is the tuning note orchestras use.
music/music-pitch.82649ce225a9: 简谱 numbered notation. Numbers instead of dots on lines. One to seven equals do to ti; dots above or below change the octave; zero is a rest. The idea came from France, Rousseau proposed numbers in seventeen forty-two, and reached China through Japan around nineteen hundred in the school-song movement 学堂乐歌.
music/music-pitch.08dcadc055d6: Don't mix up: A “third” spans three letter names but only four, major, or three, minor, half steps.
music/music-pitch.e0696147db41: Don't mix up: An octave has eight letter names but twelve half steps.

music/music-rhythm.e27c6f1cdf17: Presto. Very fast. Italian for “quickly.” At two hundred BPM a beat lasts only zero point three seconds!
music/music-rhythm.f78002d958d7: Resting heart rate. Your body’s own beat. A normal adult resting heart beats sixty to one hundred times a minute. Kids’ hearts beat a bit faster; exercise can push it above one hundred fifty.
music/music-rhythm.9d33dc0a6b6c: Meter and time signature. How beats are grouped. Top number: beats per measure. Bottom: which note gets the beat, four equals quarter. Two four, march. Three four, waltz. Four four, most pop. Six eight equals two big beats of three.
music/music-rhythm.2b68ce089c7e: Tempo. How fast the beat goes. Measured in BPM — beats per minute. Sixty BPM equals one beat per second.
music/music-rhythm.b0d3e6d4ab84: Moderato. Moderate. Neither fast nor slow. Many marches sit around one hundred ten to one hundred twenty BPM.
music/music-rhythm.b80feebb72f8: Andante. A walking pace. From the Italian for “to walk.” Most people walk at roughly one hundred to one hundred twenty steps a minute.
music/music-rhythm.71ee578144eb: 板眼. Chinese words for strong and weak beats. In Chinese opera and folk music, 板 is the strong beat, 眼 a weak beat. 一板一眼 equals two four, 一板三眼 equals four four, 有板无眼 equals one four, 散板 equals free time with no fixed beat.
music/music-rhythm.09d16631d83c: Don't mix up: six eighths is not “three quarters doubled”: six eighths feels like two big beats, three quarters feels like three.
music/music-rhythm.3074314498fa: Don't mix up: In 京剧 Peking opera the 板 is marked by the clapper 板 itself — a real wooden instrument!

physics/buoyancy.115572e38898: The model starts with a fully inflated balloon of fixed volume, two thousand cubic meters. The outside air has a density of one point two zero kilograms per cubic meter. The envelope, basket and load have a combined mass of four hundred fifty kilograms. As some air escapes during heating, the air inside gets less dense. The balloon rises when buoyancy exceeds its total weight.
physics/buoyancy.ae2abfbafcae: A hollow hull can displace enough water to support the ship. While afloat, displacement in mass units equals the total mass of the ship and its load. The model ship has an empty mass of six hundred metric tons, one metric ton equals one thousand kilograms.
physics/buoyancy.c79b398b1b98: Buoyant force, 浮力, is the upward push of a liquid or gas on an object. At rest, the scale’s pull and buoyancy together balance the block’s weight. Subtract the reading in liquid from the reading in air.
physics/buoyancy.a919b12af5aa: Read the stem at the liquid surface after the hydrometer floats freely. Its weight stays fixed, so in a denser liquid it displaces less and floats higher. The model hydrometer has a mass of sixty grams.

physics/electric-power.fabdc360d1ac: Electric power, 电功率, is how fast electrical energy is transferred. One watt is one joule per second. Rated power is the power a device uses in normal operation at its rated voltage. Actual power is the power it uses under its current operating conditions.
physics/electric-power.4eb34c39c016: A traditional test pen, 试电笔, has a large internal resistance. With enough voltage relative to earth, a tiny current can flow through the pen and return toward earth through the person holding it. That current lights the neon lamp. Choose a wire in the model.
physics/electric-power.7660066288a6: Electrical energy, 电能, tells you how much energy a device transfers. At steady power, electrical work W equals P t. In a DC circuit with steady voltage and current, W equals U I t. Subtract the earlier meter reading from the later one to find the energy used.

physics/electricity.1b7e9ee361e8: Electrons, moving charge. Tiny negative charges that flow in metal wires. The blue dots are electrons. They flow from the minus terminal, through the circuit, to the plus terminal. Scientists draw “conventional current” the other way, from plus to minus. That rule was chosen before electrons were discovered. The dots move faster when the current is bigger. Real electrons drift slowly, but the whole wire is full of them, so they all start moving together and the bulb lights instantly.
physics/electricity.add7df3286f3: Battery, cells. The energy source that pushes charges around the loop. Voltage, measured in volts, V, is the “push” a battery gives to charges. Each cell here gives one point five volts. Cells joined end-to-end, in series, add up: three cells equals four point five volts. Inside the battery, chemical energy is changed into electrical energy. Electrons leave the negative, minus, terminal, travel around the circuit, and return to the positive, plus, terminal.

physics/energy.211e11e65aad: Kinetic energy. Energy of motion. KE equals one half times m times v squared, half times mass times speed squared. Speed counts the most: twice the speed, FOUR times the KE. The cart has the most KE at the lowest point of the track, where it is fastest.
physics/energy.69d53275f194: Conservation of energy. The total never changes. Mechanical energy equals KE plus PE. Law of conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another. On this coaster: KE plus GPE plus elastic PE plus thermal energy equals the energy the lift motor put in.
physics/energy.2a0f78417ada: Gravitational potential energy. Energy stored by height. GPE equals m times g times h, mass times nine point eight newtons per kilogram times height. Units: joules, J. Twice the height, twice the GPE. Twice the mass, twice the GPE. The cart has the most GPE at the top of the start hill, where it is moving slowest.
physics/energy.196ded15f25a: Reference level, h equals zero. Where we measure height from. Gravitational PE is measured from a chosen reference level. Here it is the ground. At the ground, h equals zero, so GPE equals zero joules. You may choose any reference level, but you must use the same one for the whole problem.

physics/formula-sheet.56f192b21f4c: Buoyancy from a spring scale. Rearrange to F 浮 equals G minus T. Keep the object at rest and clear of the container. When measuring G in air, the model ignores air buoyancy.
physics/formula-sheet.c5b3e3f008c0: Density. Pair the mass and volume of the same sample. One gram per cubic centimeter equals one thousand kilograms per cubic meter.
physics/formula-sheet.60fe0417e494: Wave speed. Wavelength is the distance between neighboring crests. In a fixed medium with a fixed wave speed, increasing frequency shortens the wavelength. For light in vacuum, v is about three point zero times ten to the eighth meters per second.
physics/formula-sheet.7e426b7793dc: Electrical work from voltage and current. Use constant voltage and current. Volts times amps times seconds gives joules. The billing unit is kilowatt-hours, and one kilowatt-hour equals three point six times ten to the sixth joules.
physics/formula-sheet.3adb45efd8f9: Voltage division in series. The same current flows through both resistors. For nonzero voltage drops, U one over U two equals R one over R two. If both voltages are zero, the voltages alone give no resistance ratio.
physics/formula-sheet.33e8296657d6: Current division in parallel. Both resistors have the same voltage across them. For nonzero branch currents, I one over I two equals R two over R one. If both currents are zero, the currents alone give no resistance ratio.
physics/formula-sheet.ab10af00c76d: Convex lens, real image. This positive-distance form models a thin converging lens with a real image. The object must be farther from the lens than its focal length. At u equals two f the image is real, inverted and the same size.
physics/formula-sheet.641f8b88a5af: Electric power. Use the device’s actual terminal voltage and current. Rated power applies at the rated operating conditions. Average power is W over t.
physics/formula-sheet.6bbe7f228cde: Celsius and kelvin. Apply the offset to a temperature reading. For a change in temperature, an interval of one degree Celsius equals one kelvin.
physics/formula-sheet.d373722cea97: Energy from meter pulses. If the meter constant is given in pulses per kilowatt-hour, impulses per kilowatt-hour, or turns per kilowatt-hour, revolutions per kilowatt-hour, the quotient is in kilowatt-hours. Count the pulses or complete turns during the interval.
physics/formula-sheet.6c01cd2e1105: Contact pressure. Use the actual contact area and the perpendicular force. One square centimeter equals zero point zero zero zero one square meters.

physics/heat-transfer.f7adb9f28450: Radiation, glowing coil. Heat carried by electromagnetic waves. The red-hot coil gives off infrared radiation in all directions — hold your hand beside it, never on it, and you feel the warmth. Radiation needs no matter. That is how the Sun’s energy crosses one hundred fifty million kilometers of empty space to reach Earth. Dark, dull surfaces absorb radiation well; shiny, light surfaces reflect it.
physics/heat-transfer.9825f097fd48: Thermometer, temperature. Measures how hot or cold. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance. Faster particles equals higher temperature. Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius and freezes at zero degrees Celsius, at sea level. The liquid in the thermometer expands when it warms up, so it rises up the tube.
physics/heat-transfer.e877e4afdd31: Steam, thermal energy. Energy of moving particles. Thermal energy is the total kinetic energy of all the particles in an object. As the water gains thermal energy its molecules move faster. The fastest ones escape from the surface as water vapour. When boiling, the extra energy breaks the water molecules apart from each other instead of raising the temperature, so boiling water stays at one hundred degrees Celsius.

physics/lenses.891748e298a1: A camera lens system converges light. Here u equals sixty centimeters and f equals fifteen centimeters, so the object is beyond two F. The image is real, inverted, and smaller. Move the sensor until the rays meet on it. Dashed lines show where the rays would go without the sensor in the way.

physics/light.2806d88a8c63: Common mix-up: Rotate the mirror by ten degrees and the reflected ray turns by twenty degrees, because both angles change.
physics/light.82d6f09929d0: Laser, light source. Makes a narrow, straight beam of light. Light is an electromagnetic wave. It needs no air or water to travel, so sunlight can cross empty space to reach us. In one material, light travels in straight lines. We draw these paths as rays with arrows. Light is the fastest thing in the universe: about three hundred thousand kilometers every second in a vacuum.
physics/light.def788db9284: Normal line. An imaginary line at ninety degrees to the surface. The dashed yellow line is the normal. It is drawn wherever light hits a surface. The angle of incidence, i, and the angle of reflection or refraction, r, are measured from the normal. A ray that travels exactly along the normal does not bend when it enters glass.
physics/light.17afd7602a1b: Light ray. A model of the path light takes. The moving dots show the direction light travels. When light meets matter it can be reflected, bounce, refracted or transmitted, pass through and bend, or absorbed, turned into heat. You see an object when light from it, made or reflected, enters your eyes.
physics/light.e510675c6232: Glass block. Refraction: light bends when its speed changes. Light slows from about three hundred thousand kilometers per second in air to about two hundred thousand kilometers per second in glass. Entering glass, fast, slow, the ray bends TOWARD the normal. Leaving, slow, fast, it bends AWAY. With parallel sides, the ray comes out parallel to the way it went in, just shifted sideways. If light inside glass hits the surface at a big angle, more than about forty-two degrees, it cannot escape: total internal reflection. Optical fibers use this.

physics/magnetism.84683d77a5dd: Iron core, nail. Makes the coil’s field much stronger. Iron inside the coil becomes magnetized and adds its own field. An iron core can make an electromagnet hundreds of times stronger. This model uses ten times. Soft iron loses its magnetism quickly when the current stops, which is perfect for an electromagnet.

physics/motion.e689011cb7fd: Velocity. Speed in a direction. Velocity is speed together with its direction, for example ten meters per second east. The green arrow above each car shows its velocity: a longer arrow means faster, and it points the way the car moves. When a car reverses, its velocity becomes negative: the arrow flips to point backwards.
physics/motion.6fa1cf86ea85: Speed. How fast: distance divided by time. Speed equals distance divided by time. The SI unit is meters per second, meters per second. Average speed equals total distance divided by total time. Instantaneous speed is the speed at one moment, like a speedometer reading. Ten meters per second is thirty-six kilometers per hour, about as fast as a quick bicycle.
physics/motion.b6d41af05083: Common mix-up: A car driving around a curve at a steady twenty meters per second has a constant speed but a CHANGING velocity, because its direction keeps changing.
physics/motion.ddcc1d738af4: Acceleration. How fast velocity changes. Acceleration equals change in velocity divided by time: a equals the quantity v end minus v start, divided by t. Unit: meters per second squared, meters per second, every second. a equals two point five meters per second squared means the velocity grows by two point five meters per second every second. Slowing down is also acceleration, pointing backwards, negative. Turning is acceleration too.
physics/motion.7eca254420a9: Common mix-up: Speed has no direction. Ten meters per second north and ten meters per second south are the same SPEED but different VELOCITIES.
physics/motion.1f70c606ee2e: Common mix-up: Run one four hundred meter lap and stop where you began: distance equals four hundred meters, displacement equals zero meters. Turn on “Allow reversing” to see this on the track.
physics/motion.7f3559433bad: Displacement. Change in position, with a direction. Displacement tells how far and in which direction you end up from your starting point. The cyan arrow on the track points from the start line to each car: that is the car’s displacement. If you come back to where you started, your displacement is zero meters, even though your distance is not.
physics/motion.7cb98932301a: Common mix-up: Acceleration does not mean “going fast”. A car cruising at a steady thirty meters per second has ZERO acceleration.
physics/motion.59b7f3e6008d: Distance. How much ground is covered. Distance is the total length of the path an object travels. Its SI unit is the meter, meter. Distance never goes down: even driving backwards adds to it, like a car’s odometer. The marker posts on this track are ten meters apart, and the whole strip is one hundred meters long.

physics/newtons-laws.7197eb7b86a3: Action-reaction pair, third law. Forces always come in equal, opposite pairs. Newton’s third law: when object A pushes on object B, B pushes back on A with a force of equal size in the opposite direction. The spring pushes the left cart left with forty newtons and the right cart right with forty newtons, at the same time. Equal forces, but the lighter cart gets the bigger acceleration, a equals F divided by m, so it speeds away faster.
physics/newtons-laws.268083c893a0: Mass. Amount of matter equals amount of inertia. Mass is how much matter an object has, measured in kilograms, kilograms. Each gray block on a cart is one kilogram. More mass means more inertia: it is harder to speed up, slow down or turn. With the same force, a four kilogram cart gets only one quarter of the acceleration of a one kilogram cart.
physics/newtons-laws.c8aeedadd89c: Inertia, first law. Objects keep doing what they are doing. Newton’s first law: an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion keeps moving at the same speed and direction, unless an unbalanced force acts on it. Inertia is this tendency to resist changes in motion. More mass equals more inertia. In the fast yank, the cloth’s friction acts for only a fraction of a second, so the dishes barely move.
physics/newtons-laws.6f946bb42fed: Weight, gravity. W equals m times g. Weight is the force of gravity on a mass: W equals m times g. On Earth g equals nine point eight newtons per kilogram. The spring scale holds a one kilogram mass: it reads nine point eight newtons on Earth, one point six newtons on the Moon, twenty-four point eight newtons on Jupiter. Mass, kilograms, stays the same everywhere; weight, newtons, changes with the planet.
physics/newtons-laws.d013d77355a6: Friction from the cloth. The only sideways force on the dishes. Friction between cloth and dish can give the dish at most about mu times g, about zero point five times nine point eight, about four point nine meters per second squared of acceleration. Pull the cloth more gently than that and the dishes ride along with it, and fall off the edge! Yank harder and the cloth slides out from under them; the dishes only get a short, weak tug.
physics/newtons-laws.a627ec5952bd: Acceleration. a equals F divided by m. The orange arrow appears only while the push acts: acceleration happens only when there is a net force. a equals ten newtons divided by two kilograms equals five meters per second squared. The velocity grows by five meters per second every second of pushing. Acceleration is always in the same direction as the net force.
physics/newtons-laws.6c4647c0012f: Common mix-up: When the push stops, the cart does NOT stop. On a frictionless track it keeps rolling at a constant velocity, first law.
physics/newtons-laws.aa7b7344a498: Net force, the push. An unbalanced force changes motion. Force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons, newtons. One newton is about the weight of a small apple. The red arrow is the push. It lasts zero point five seconds; after that the net force is zero. Newton’s second law: F equals m times a, so a equals F divided by m. Double the force, double the acceleration.

physics/ohms-law.829e5bfc6605: Ohm’s law is written I equals U over R. At constant resistance, current is proportional to voltage. At a fixed voltage, current is inversely proportional to resistance. A bulb’s filament usually gets hotter as the voltage rises, so its resistance increases. The dashed curve is an illustrative model.

physics/phase-changes.4bece561e69f: At one atmosphere, pure ice melts at about zero degrees Celsius, thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit, and pure water boils at about one hundred degrees Celsius, two hundred twelve degrees Fahrenheit. On each plateau, the sample still absorbs heat. The share of the mass in each phase changes while the temperature stays steady. At the same pressure, pure water freezes at about zero degrees Celsius and releases heat as it freezes.
physics/phase-changes.51b60b8a0cea: Estimate the temperature and choose a suitable range. Check the unit and the value of one small division. Each small interval here is two degrees Celsius. Fully immerse the bulb in the liquid. Keep the bulb clear of the container’s bottom and sides. Wait for the reading to stabilize. Keep the bulb immersed and read with your eyes level with the top of the liquid column.

physics/pressure.2dfb0e2f217f: Water pushes on the probe’s flexible membrane and raises the air pressure in the hose. The water falls on the connected side and rises on the open side. Read the vertical difference delta H. In this ideal model, both liquids are water, so delta H equals the probe depth.
physics/pressure.452f0a0166d1: Average pressure, 压强, is perpendicular force F divided by contact area S. The force acts at right angles to the surface. Keep the force fixed and compare the marks made by the three faces.

physics/simple-machines.9a5795c55af4: Pulley. A grooved wheel with a rope. A fixed pulley, attached to the ceiling, only changes the direction of your pull: MA equals one. A movable pulley rides up with the load and halves the force: MA equals two. A block and tackle combines pulleys: MA equals the number of rope strands holding up the load.
physics/simple-machines.43827a5f5046: Mechanical advantage and work. How many times a machine multiplies your force. Mechanical advantage, MA, equals output force divided by input force. MA four means one hundred newtons of effort lifts a four hundred newton load. Work equals force times distance, measured in joules, joules. One joule equals one newton times one meter. With MA four you pull four meters of rope to lift the load one meter: the work is the same, ideal machine.
physics/simple-machines.cb968e57239e: Lever. A rigid bar that turns on a fulcrum. A lever is a stiff bar that pivots on a point called the fulcrum. Class one: fulcrum in the middle, seesaw, crowbar, scissors. Class two: load in the middle, wheelbarrow, bottle opener. Class three: effort in the middle, tweezers, broom, your forearm. Law of the lever: effort times effort arm equals load times load arm.
physics/simple-machines.e7b4a2b71bd5: Common mix-up: Machines do NOT reduce the work you do! If a machine cuts your force to one quarter, you must move four times as far. Work equals force times distance stays the same, ideally; in real life friction makes it a little more.
physics/simple-machines.d72b6dadaa3f: Common mix-up: Not every lever makes work easier on your muscles. A class three lever needs MORE force than the load, but the load end moves farther and faster.
physics/simple-machines.320e4478a204: Common mix-up: No machine gives more work out than you put in. Real machines lose some work to friction, so efficiency is always below one hundred percent.
physics/simple-machines.1f0c046ac907: Inclined plane. A ramp: less force over a longer distance. An inclined plane is a flat sloping surface, like a ramp. Pushing a load up a ramp takes less force than lifting it straight up, but you move it farther. Ideal MA equals ramp length divided by height. A four meter ramp up to one meter has MA four.
physics/simple-machines.675a5c84f9e2: Load and load arm. The weight you want to move. The load, resistance, is the force the machine works against, here the weight of the crate: W equals m times g. The load arm is the distance from the fulcrum to the load. A twenty kilogram crate weighs twenty times nine point eight equals one hundred ninety-six newtons.

physics/sound.37b85e5a1e4e: Air molecules, the medium. Pass the vibration along. Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs a medium — a solid, liquid or gas — to travel through. Each molecule just jiggles back and forth around its place and bumps the next one. The molecules do not fly from the speaker to your ear. Sound travels faster in liquids and fastest in solids, because their particles are closer together: air about three hundred forty-three meters per second, water about one thousand four hundred eighty meters per second, steel about five thousand nine hundred sixty meters per second.
physics/sound.3a403e374348: Ear canal. Carries sound to the eardrum. The ear canal is a tube about two point five centimeters long that leads from the outer ear to the eardrum. It contains earwax, which traps dust and protects the ear. Never push objects into your ear canal: you could damage the eardrum.
physics/sound.4bb21f5af47d: Ossicles, hammer, anvil, stirrup. Amplify the vibrations. Three tiny bones in the middle ear: the hammer, malleus, anvil, incus, and stirrup, stapes. They act like levers, passing the vibrations from the eardrum to the cochlea and making them stronger. The stirrup is the smallest bone in the human body — about three millimeters long.

physics/specific-heat.46cd07035ad5: The exhaust valve opens and the intake valve stays closed. The rising piston pushes burned gases out of the cylinder. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice, seven hundred twenty degrees, per cycle, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.
physics/specific-heat.e974bf6fda99: The intake valve opens and the exhaust valve stays closed. The piston moves down, drawing an air-fuel mixture into the cylinder. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice, seven hundred twenty degrees, per cycle, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.
physics/specific-heat.d58717832944: Temperature. A measure of how hot or cold something is. At a higher temperature, particles generally move more vigorously. Even particles in a solid keep vibrating. Internal energy, nèinéng. Add the energy from particles’ motion to the potential energy from their interactions to get the object’s internal energy. Internal energy depends on factors such as temperature, mass, and state. Ice has internal energy, too. Heat, rèliàng. Energy transferred because of a temperature difference, measured in joules, joules. The net transfer by heat is from higher to lower temperature. Molecules are always moving randomly. During diffusion, kuòsàn, 扩散, particles move in all directions, with an overall spread from higher to lower concentration. They keep moving after the gases are mixed. Molecules also exert forces on one another. At very close range they repel, and at somewhat greater distances attraction can hold them together.
physics/specific-heat.3887c10466fd: A fuel’s heating value, rèzhí, 热值, q, is the energy released per unit mass in complete combustion, measured in joules per kilogram. Use the heating value given in a calculation problem. Efficiency eta is useful work W divided by the energy Q released by complete combustion. The remaining energy still counts in the total. Much of it leaves in hot exhaust or through the cooling system. Friction also converts some mechanical energy into internal energy.
physics/specific-heat.6e2c3f632383: Both valves stay closed. Combustion raises the gas temperature and pressure. The expanding gas pushes the piston down and does work on it, turning the crankshaft. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice, seven hundred twenty degrees, per cycle, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.
physics/specific-heat.ea1f913e6462: Specific heat capacity, bǐrèróng, 比热容, c, is the energy needed to warm one kilogram of a material by one degree Celsius. We use about four thousand two hundred joules per kilogram degree Celsius for water and about eight hundred joules per kilogram degree Celsius for dry sand. For equal masses given equal energy, the sample with the larger c warms less.
physics/specific-heat.b3cb6f9112a1: Both valves are closed. The piston moves up and does work on the mixture, raising its pressure and temperature. The spark plug fires near the end. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice, seven hundred twenty degrees, per cycle, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.

physics/waves.32c4ff092d4e: Amplitude. How big the vibration is. Amplitude is the distance from the rest position to a crest, or to a trough. Bigger amplitude equals more energy. The energy grows with the amplitude squared: double A, four times the energy. For sound, larger amplitude means louder; for light, brighter; for water, taller waves.
physics/waves.aa525c2e8fd7: Vibrating source, frequency. Where every wave begins. Every wave starts with a vibration: a hand shaking a rope, a speaker cone, a pebble dropped in a pond. Frequency, f, is the number of complete waves made — or passing a point — each second. Unit: hertz, hertz. One hertz equals one wave per second. Period T equals one divided by f is the time for one complete wave. Wave speed v equals f times lambda.

physics/work-power.8bfd897ce897: Trace the rope and count the n segments that pull upward directly on the load or moving block. The supporting strands are vertical and the rope does not stretch. For a steady lift, ignore rope weight, pulley weight, and friction. Then all strands have the same tension, and the pull is G over n. As the load rises by h, the combined change in supporting rope length is n h, so the free end has to move n h.

politics/china-world.634608aa3ce6: One hundred forty-two kilometers in Indonesia, trains at three hundred fifty kilometers per hour, opened October twenty twenty-three.
politics/china-world.13c7366b7e56: Medical teams abroad, Algeria, nineteen sixty-three. Doctors sent abroad for sixty years. China sent its first medical team to Algeria in nineteen sixty-three. Since then teams have worked in more than seventy countries, mostly in Africa, treating about two hundred ninety million patients, figure as of twenty twenty-three. During COVID nineteen China sent medical supplies and vaccines to many countries.
politics/china-world.3da6c6cd60df: China at the United Nations. A permanent member of the Security Council. In nineteen seventy-one the UN General Assembly restored the lawful seat of the People’s Republic of China. China is one of five permanent members of the Security Council and the second-largest payer of the UN budget. Textbook: China is a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development and a defender of international order.
politics/china-world.6cd182c1bdc0: Proposed by China in twenty thirteen, it revives the idea of the ancient Silk Road: building railways, ports and trade links together with other countries.
politics/china-world.a150133a4810: Xi’an. A stop on the “Belt”. Start of the ancient Silk Road, when it was the Han and Tang capital Chang’an. In one hundred thirty-eight B C E the envoy Zhang Qian set out west from here.
politics/china-world.d808457d741c: China-Laos Railway. From “land-locked” to “land-linked”. One thousand thirty-five kilometers from Kunming in China to Vientiane, capital of Laos; opened December twenty twenty-one. Laos has no coast. The railway gives it a fast link to ports and markets. It crosses mountains through one hundred sixty-seven tunnels.
politics/china-world.c685051a0fbf: The Belt and Road. One belt on land, one road at sea. Proposed by China in twenty thirteen, it revives the idea of the ancient Silk Road: building railways, ports and trade links together with other countries. More than one hundred fifty countries have signed cooperation documents. Click the dots, stops, and gold diamonds, China’s contributions. Use the switches and drag the year.
politics/china-world.a623e3e67646: Memory hook: Since nineteen sixty-three, doctors without a break.
politics/china-world.4756af748579: Quanzhou. A port on the “Road”. One of the world’s great ports in the Song and Yuan dynasties, a UNESCO World Heritage site since twenty twenty-one.
politics/china-world.5ccf5828129d: Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway. Southeast Asia’s first high-speed line. One hundred forty-two kilometers in Indonesia, trains at three hundred fifty kilometers per hour, opened October twenty twenty-three. The trip between Jakarta and Bandung fell from over three hours to about forty minutes. Built jointly by Indonesian and Chinese companies using Chinese high-speed rail technology.
politics/china-world.1ce5cf719bec: More than one hundred fifty countries have signed cooperation documents.
politics/china-world.d2c7e75d0175: The trip between Jakarta and Bandung fell from over three hours to about forty minutes.
politics/china-world.1a6d023d082f: Mombasa-Nairobi Railway, Kenya. Kenya’s first new railway in a century. About four hundred eighty kilometers, built by a Chinese company and opened in twenty seventeen. It cut the trip from the port of Mombasa to the capital Nairobi from over ten hours to about five. Bridges and underpasses let giraffes and elephants cross the line in Tsavo National Park.
politics/china-world.93d6cbe0812a: Piraeus, Athens. A port on the “Road”. Greece’s main port. A Chinese shipping company has run its container terminals since two thousand nine and it became one of the Mediterranean’s busiest.
politics/china-world.70429ee632c5: “Compare with the US” cards are factual and say plainly where views differ — a good chance to compare sources. Suggested flow: hook “where did your phone come from?”, three minutes, map and year slider, fifteen minutes, idea web and matching, ten minutes, case files, ten minutes, quiz and sorting, seven minutes.
politics/china-world.c7bf82c4fa49: Like China’s grade-nine exam, 中考: some questions start with a short “material” to analyse.
politics/china-world.7d359ae17105: Case one, The sneaker factory. Your uncle’s factory in Fujian makes sneakers for brands in Europe and America. This year a country far away raises its import taxes, and orders fall by a third.
politics/china-world.aa649536a988: Moscow. Its fortress, the Kremlin, and Red Square are at the centre. In nineteen forty-one the German army was stopped just outside the city.
politics/china-world.8c970b375a65: Mombasa. A port on the “Road”. Kenya’s port. Zheng He’s fleet reached this coast in the fourteen hundreds; today a Chinese-built railway starts here.
politics/china-world.7d2ee002f50e: UN peacekeepers, South Sudan. The “blue helmets”. China first sent military observers to a UN mission in nineteen ninety; since then it has sent more than fifty thousand peacekeepers. Among the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, China sends the most peacekeepers; it is the second-largest payer of peacekeeping costs. In South Sudan, Chinese units protect civilians, build roads and run a hospital.
politics/china-world.9df6b007d2b4: Question one of ten. A phone designed in one country, with parts from ten others, assembled in a third, shows…
politics/china-world.6909077f8a74: Samarkand. A stop on the “Belt”. A two thousand seven hundred-year-old trading city in Uzbekistan, famous on the old Silk Road.
politics/china-world.a50a20920cb0: China-Europe freight trains. A “steel camel caravan” across Eurasia. The first train ran from Chongqing to Duisburg in twenty eleven, taking about sixteen days — far quicker than by sea. By twenty twenty-four more than one hundred thousand trains had run, linking over two hundred European cities. They carry electronics and cars west; wine, timber and machinery east.
politics/china-world.c303545f5188: This lesson follows China’s national curriculum standard for Morality and Rule of Law, twenty twenty-two edition; “national conditions” theme: world trends, a community with a shared future for humanity, China’s role in international affairs, and the wording of the national unified textbook “道德与法治” Grade nine Volume two: Unit one “Our Shared World”, Lessons one to two, and Unit two “China on the World Stage”, Lessons three to four.
politics/china-world.9c25e47bce1b: Board one: click stops and projects on the map, switch the land and sea routes on and off, and drag the years to watch events appear. Board two: open eight key ideas. Board three: match global problems to joint action.
politics/china-world.48a43568ab00: Almaty. A stop on the “Belt”. Largest city of Kazakhstan — the country where the “Silk Road Economic Belt” was first proposed in twenty thirteen.
politics/china-world.8b19376237a5: Venice. A stop on the “Belt”. Home of Marco Polo, who travelled to China in the twelve hundreds. On the schematic map the land and sea routes meet here.
politics/china-world.86fa22286a65: Guangzhou. A port on the “Road”. A trading port for over two thousand years, and still one of the busiest on Earth.

politics/constitution.07db550beb88: Respecting and protecting human rights. “The state respects and protects human rights.” The textbook defines human rights as the rights a person should have as a human being; their goal is each person’s free and all-round development. This sentence was written into the Constitution in two thousand four and is a constitutional principle. Who has them: every citizen — with special care for women, minors, the elderly and people with disabilities. What they cover: equality, political rights, personal freedom, and economic, social, cultural and educational rights.
politics/constitution.4b321c6a4628: Tian’anmen. Gate of the Ming and Qing imperial city; founding ceremony of the PRC, October first, nineteen forty-nine. On October first, nineteen forty-nine, Chairman Mao Zedong stood on this gate tower and proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China. The square in front can hold about a million people.
politics/constitution.1a8f439908af: Laws. Ordinary laws are written on the basis of the Constitution and fill in its details. The National People’s Congress, 全国人民代表大会, NPC, and its Standing Committee make China’s national laws. Many laws open with the line “This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution”. Examples: the Civil Code, the Criminal Law, the Compulsory Education Law, the Law on the Protection of Minors.
politics/constitution.bb404c37b4f9: Administrative regulations. Rules made by the State Council in line with the Constitution and the laws. The State Council, 国务院, is the central government and the highest administrative organ. Examples: the Regulations on School Bus Safety; the Regulations on Protecting Minors Online. They may not go against the Constitution or the laws.
politics/constitution.cc84ceb38fef: Constitution Day and the oath. December fourth is National Constitution Day in China. The current Constitution was adopted on December fourth, nineteen eighty-two; since twenty fourteen that date is National Constitution Day. Schools hold readings and class meetings about the Constitution that day. State officials must publicly swear an oath to the Constitution when they take office, 宪法宣誓. The oath begins: “I pledge to be loyal to the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China, safeguard its authority and perform my legal duties…”

politics/core-values.19aca6ce8afd: Question one of ten. Material: On the eve of the Spring Festival, hundreds of millions of people travel home for a reunion dinner; children bow to grandparents and receive red envelopes. Which traditional virtue stands out?
politics/core-values.963793425202: The twenty-four characters, their three levels, value goals of the nation, value orientation of society, value standards for citizens, and the definition of the national spirit are given in the textbook’s own wording.
politics/core-values.67b394c14a56: Case one, The wallet on the playground. After PE you find a wallet behind the goal: three hundred yuan and a student ID card inside. Nobody saw you pick it up.
politics/core-values.53e956dea9ba: The Core Socialist Values. Three levels, four words each. Set out nationally in twenty twelve, the twelve words answer three questions: what kind of country, what kind of society, what kind of citizen? Tap a word, then tap the level you think it belongs to, or drag it. When a tile is placed, click it to see what it means and what it looks like at school.
politics/core-values.b478d42022b2: Listen: The last card is a recording of the guqin, 古琴, a seven-string zither played for over three thousand years and listed by UNESCO as world intangible heritage in two thousand three. The tune, “Three Refrains on Yang Pass,” sets a Tang-dynasty farewell poem. Press play — nothing starts by itself.
politics/core-values.22ce8d8edbab: Memory hook: Nation: 富强 民主 文明 和谐, Society: 自由 平等 公正 法治, Citizen: 爱国 敬业 诚信 友善
politics/core-values.4e545e97be3f: Like the grade-nine exam in China, 中考: some questions start with a short “material” to analyse.
politics/core-values.b3154783e42b: Common mix-up: Students often put 民主, democracy, and 法治, rule of law, on the wrong level. Democracy is a goal of the nation; rule of law is an orientation of society.
politics/core-values.f2c585781089: Board one: sort the twelve words into three levels. Board two: drag the time slider to follow Chinese culture through three thousand years.
politics/core-values.af050a4f1255: Suggested flow: hook “sum up your country in twelve words”, five minutes, build board one and open every tile, twelve minutes, time slider and the culture, virtue, spirit, confidence chain, eight minutes, everyday choices, ten minutes, listen to the guqin, browse photos, take the quiz, ten minutes.
politics/core-values.b588b999739f: This lesson follows China’s national curriculum standard for Morality and Rule of Law, twenty twenty-two edition; themes “education in fine traditional Chinese culture” and “national conditions”, and the wording of the national unified textbook “道德与法治” Grade nine Volume one, Unit three “Civilisation and Homeland”, Lesson five “Guarding Our Spiritual Home”.
politics/core-values.a670d686c6f9: Set out nationally in twenty twelve, the twelve words answer three questions: what kind of country, what kind of society, what kind of citizen?
politics/core-values.0a77a9a95abe: If you had to sum up what your country stands for in just twelve words, which would you pick? China did exactly that: twenty-four Chinese characters making twelve two-character words, called the Core Socialist Values, 社会主义核心价值观. You will see them on posters in every Chinese city and school. Where do they come from, and what do they have to do with five thousand years of culture?

politics/development.c765e245ce94: Beijing South Railway Station. A huge high-speed rail station opened in two thousand eight; the Beijing-Shanghai and Beijing-Tianjin lines start here.
politics/development.8ebf05dae733: Common mix-up: Do not mix up a “basic state policy”, 基本国策, for example, saving resources and protecting the environment, with a “strategy”, 战略, for example, innovation-driven development.
politics/development.53c9b4b6afc1: Three sliders, three curves. A simplified model — not real data. Start with all three sliders at zero: growth looks great at first. Now drag the year to twenty. Raise “green” and “innovation”: the first years are slower. Why? What happens later? Challenge: finish year twenty with the economy above two hundred fifty, the environment above sixty and sharing above sixty.

politics/rights-duties.d94bd3762604: Political rights and freedoms. The rights that let citizens take part in the country’s political life. Voting and standing for election: every citizen aged eighteen or over, whatever their ethnic group, sex, job, family background, religion, education, property or length of residence, except people the law has deprived of political rights. Political freedoms: speech, the press, assembly, association, procession and demonstration. The right to supervise, 监督权: citizens may criticise and make suggestions to any state organ or official, and may report officials who break the law.
politics/rights-duties.d7d8563a060c: Social, economic, cultural and educational rights. The rights that protect a citizen’s living, working and learning. Property: a citizen’s lawful private property may not be violated — you may own, use, benefit from and dispose of it, and inherit. Material help, 物质帮助权: citizens who are old, ill or unable to work have the right to help from the state and society. Work and education belong here too — and they are also duties, see the “both” bar. Citizens are free to do scientific research, create literature and art, and take part in other cultural activities.
politics/rights-duties.2945c08bcd1f: How to defend a right. When a right is harmed, defend it through lawful steps. One, Negotiate, 协商: talk it out directly with the other side. Two, Mediation, 调解: a neutral third party, such as a people’s mediation committee, helps both sides agree. Three, Arbitration, 仲裁: an arbitration body gives a binding decision. Four, Lawsuit, 诉讼: go to court. The textbook calls it the most formal and authoritative way — “the last line of defence”.

politics/rule-of-law.e3a95a96c8e7: The staircase of offences. Three kinds of unlawful act. An unlawful act is one that breaks the law and so must bear legal responsibility. By which law is broken, there are three kinds: civil, administrative and criminal. Civil and administrative offences are “ordinary offences”, 一般违法. Criminal offences are crimes, 犯罪 — the most harmful. Drag the slider to watch one quarrel climb the stairs.
politics/rule-of-law.dc102655ae11: Six shields around every minor. Why do minors get special protection? Minors are still growing in body and mind; they lack experience and self-protection ability, and are easily harmed. They are the future of the country, so the state gives them special, priority protection. China’s Law on the Protection of Minors, 未成年人保护法, names six kinds of protection. Click all six sectors.

politics/state-organs.3cec25ffb063: National Supervisory Commission. Supervisory commissions are the state’s supervisory organs; the National Supervisory Commission is the highest one. Added to the Constitution by the twenty eighteen amendment. It supervises all public employees who exercise public power. Three duties: supervise, investigate, and deal with, 监督, 调查, 处置, duty-related violations and crimes such as bribery. It uses its power independently according to law, free from interference by administrative organs, organisations or individuals.
politics/state-organs.88ecf4558f54: State Council. The State Council, that is, the Central People’s Government, is the executive body of the highest organ of state power and the highest administrative organ. Led by the Premier, 总理, under the “Premier responsibility system”. Runs the country’s administration: the economy, education, science, health, the environment and more. Makes administrative regulations in line with the Constitution and the laws. Local people’s governments are the local administrative organs; all of them are under the State Council’s unified leadership. Governments must act according to law, 依法行政.
politics/state-organs.e6ed85ed7760: Local levels — and the armed forces. The same pattern repeats at each level: province, city, county, township. Each level has a people’s congress and a people’s government. From county level up there are also a supervisory commission, a court and a procuratorate. Each local organ is created by the congress at its own level, answers to it and is supervised by it. The Constitution also sets up the Central Military Commission, 中央军事委员会, which leads the country’s armed forces.
politics/state-organs.112e28a2f3ba: National People’s Congress. The National People’s Congress, NPC, is the highest organ of state power. Legislative power: amends the Constitution; makes and amends basic laws. Power to decide: approves national plans and budgets and other major matters. Power to appoint and remove: elects or decides on the top leaders of the other state organs — and can remove them. Power to supervise: watches over the Constitution and the work of the other organs. Its Standing Committee, 常务委员会, is its permanent body and works when the NPC is not in session. Local people’s congresses are the local organs of state power.
politics/state-organs.8677cb1740db: Watch out: Supervisory, 监察, is not procuratorial, 检察: the commission investigates officials; the procuratorate prosecutes in court.

politics/state-system.8cacd7204c09: The socialist market economy. It joins the socialist system with a market economy. The market plays the decisive role in deciding where resources go. The government also plays its role — planning, regulating, keeping competition fair. “The state practises a socialist market economy” has been in the Constitution since nineteen ninety-three.
politics/state-system.c8e6fe43d7a1: Community-level self-governance. People in villages and city neighbourhoods run their own community affairs. Villagers’ committees, 村民委员会, and urban residents’ committees, 居民委员会, are self-governing organisations of local people. Residents elect the committee members directly. The idea: self-management, self-education, self-service and self-supervision. Typical jobs: settling neighbours’ disputes, public hygiene, deciding how to use collective funds.
politics/state-system.37dc9712a422: Multi-party cooperation and political consultation. Led by the Communist Party of China, CPC; a basic political system of China. The CPC is the governing party. Eight other parties, “democratic parties”, are participating parties: they take part in state affairs. They work with the CPC as partners — the textbook calls them friendly parties, not opposition parties. Guiding principle: “long-term coexistence, mutual supervision, sincerity with each other, sharing weal and woe”. The Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, 人民政协, CPPCC, is the main body for this cooperation: it consults, supervises democratically, and takes part in discussing state affairs.
politics/state-system.5a09519bbb3b: Regional ethnic autonomy. Under the unified leadership of the state, areas where minority ethnic groups live in concentrated communities practise regional autonomy. China has fifty-six ethnic groups; the Constitution says all are equal. Autonomous areas come in three sizes: autonomous regions, prefectures and counties. The five autonomous regions are Inner Mongolia, Xinjiang, Guangxi, Ningxia and Tibet. Their people’s congresses and governments can make rules that fit local ethnic customs and culture. Every autonomous area is an inseparable part of the People’s Republic of China.

ushistory/us-civilrights.2785c0e336f7: Greensboro sit-ins. February first, nineteen sixty, Greensboro, North Carolina. Four Black college students sat at the “whites only” lunch counter at Woolworth’s and politely asked to be served. They were refused — and came back the next day with more students. Sit-ins, 静坐, spread to dozens of cities within weeks. In April, students founded Snick, the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee. In July nineteen sixty the Greensboro Woolworth’s served Black customers at the counter. Part of that counter is now in the Smithsonian.
ushistory/us-civilrights.bd45e23bd6d1: Brown versus Board of Education. May seventeenth, nineteen fifty-four, Topeka, Kansas. Linda Brown, a Black third-grader, had to travel far to a Black school although a white school was much closer. Her father joined an NAACP lawsuit. NAACP lawyer Thurgood Marshall argued the case, with four others combined, before the Supreme Court. All nine justices agreed: “separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.” School segregation was unconstitutional.
ushistory/us-civilrights.d260227dc728: Freedom Rides. May nineteen sixty-one, Washington, D.C., the Deep South. The Supreme Court had banned segregation on interstate buses and in their stations, but Southern states ignored it. Black and white “Freedom Riders” rode buses together from Washington into the South to test the law. Near Anniston, Alabama, a mob burned one bus; riders were beaten in Birmingham and Montgomery. More riders kept coming. In September nineteen sixty-one the Interstate Commerce Commission ordered segregation signs removed from bus stations.
ushistory/us-civilrights.d62d5114a25d: Don't mix up: The March on Washington happened in nineteen sixty-three; the Civil Rights Act it pushed for was signed in nineteen sixty-four.
ushistory/us-civilrights.18589fb54598: Memphis, nineteen sixty-eight. April fourth, nineteen sixty-eight, Memphis, Tennessee. King went to Memphis to support Black sanitation workers on strike for fair pay and safe working conditions, “I AM A MAN” signs. On April fourth, nineteen sixty-eight, he was assassinated at the Lorraine Motel. He was thirty-nine. The nation mourned. A week later Congress passed the Fair Housing Act, banning discrimination in selling and renting homes. Today the motel is the National Civil Rights Museum.
ushistory/us-civilrights.583eba775894: Atlanta: Dr. King’s hometown. SCLC founded nineteen fifty-seven, Atlanta, Georgia. Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta on January fifteenth, nineteen twenty-nine, and preached at Ebenezer Baptist Church. In nineteen fifty-seven King and other ministers founded the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, SCLC, based in Atlanta, to organize nonviolent protest. In nineteen sixty Atlanta’s college students held their own sit-ins. Today his birth home is part of a National Historical Park.
ushistory/us-civilrights.afae67aa1b42: Don't mix up: The Voting Rights Act, nineteen sixty-five, protected voting; the Civil Rights Act, nineteen sixty-four, ended segregation in public places.
ushistory/us-civilrights.a1813fe69b61: The Little Rock Nine. September nineteen fifty-seven, Little Rock, Arkansas. Nine Black students enrolled at all-white Central High School to carry out the Brown decision. Arkansas Governor Orval Faubus sent the state National Guard to keep them out, and an angry crowd gathered. President Eisenhower sent soldiers of the one hundred first Airborne Division to escort the students — the federal government enforcing the Supreme Court’s ruling.
ushistory/us-civilrights.eb693f99d7a0: The Albany Movement. Nineteen sixty-one to nineteen sixty-two, Albany, Georgia. Students, churches and the NAACP in Albany, Georgia, protested segregation across the whole city at once — buses, parks, libraries, stores. Hundreds were arrested; Dr. King was jailed there too. The police chief avoided violent scenes, so the nation paid less attention. Albany did not win quick victories, but leaders learned to focus on one target — a lesson they used in Birmingham.
ushistory/us-civilrights.5bcb2ece19b0: The Birmingham Campaign. April to May nineteen sixty-three, Birmingham, Alabama. Birmingham was one of the most segregated cities in America. Protesters held marches and sit-ins, and boycotted downtown stores. Jailed for marching, King wrote the “Letter from Birmingham Jail”, explaining why people could not keep waiting for justice. In May, children and teenagers marched. Police used fire hoses and dogs on them. TV pictures shocked the nation; in June President Kennedy proposed a civil rights bill. In September a bomb at the Sixteenth Street Baptist Church killed four girls.
ushistory/us-civilrights.d03569b3a07e: Don't mix up: The “Letter from Birmingham Jail”, April nineteen sixty-three, is different from the “I Have a Dream” speech, August nineteen sixty-three, Washington.
ushistory/us-civilrights.01ea8fd31634: Montgomery Bus Boycott. The fifth of December, nineteen fifty-five, to the twentieth of December, nineteen fifty-six, Montgomery, Alabama. The first of December, nineteen fifty-five: Rosa Parks refused to give her bus seat to a white man and was arrested. Black citizens stayed off the buses for three hundred eighty-one days. They walked, shared rides and organized a carpool system. A young pastor, Martin Luther King Jr., led the Montgomery Improvement Association. In nineteen fifty-six the Supreme Court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional; Montgomery’s buses were integrated in December nineteen fifty-six.
ushistory/us-civilrights.c5df7c42fe6d: Don't mix up: Brown overturned “separate but equal”, from Plessy versus Ferguson, eighteen ninety-six, for public schools — it was a court ruling, not a law passed by Congress.
ushistory/us-civilrights.26258d20797d: March on Washington. The twenty-eighth of August, nineteen sixty-three, Washington, D.C. About two hundred fifty thousand people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial for the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom — one of the largest protests in US history at the time. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his “I Have a Dream” speech. A young John Lewis, later a congressman from Georgia, also spoke. The march built support for the civil rights bill. On the second of July, nineteen sixty-four, President Lyndon Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, banning segregation in public places and job discrimination.
ushistory/us-civilrights.156c4263c76f: Don't mix up: The Freedom Rides, nineteen sixty-one, were about interstate buses and stations; the Montgomery boycott, nineteen fifty-five, was about city buses.
ushistory/us-civilrights.563b6a8e47e7: Selma to Montgomery. March nineteen sixty-five, Selma, Montgomery, Alabama. In Selma, only a tiny share of Black adults were allowed to register to vote. On the seventh of March, nineteen sixty-five, “Bloody Sunday”, state troopers attacked peaceful marchers, led by John Lewis and Hosea Williams, on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. Two weeks later, protected by federal troops, thousands marched fifty-four miles, eighty-seven kilometers, to Montgomery. On the sixth of August, nineteen sixty-five, Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act, 选举权法.

ushistory/us-civilwar.0a6074004153: Appomattox Court House. The ninth of April, eighteen sixty-five, Virginia. Lee surrenders to Grant. Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant in the parlour of Wilmer McLean’s house. Grant let Lee’s soldiers go home and keep their horses for spring planting. Other Confederate armies surrendered in the following weeks.
ushistory/us-civilwar.f058fa58928d: Shiloh. The sixth to the seventh of April, eighteen sixty-two, Tennessee. Union victory. A surprise attack on General Ulysses S. Grant’s army; Grant held on and won on the second day. About twenty-three thousand soldiers were killed, wounded or missing — a shock to both sides about the cost of the war.
ushistory/us-civilwar.2e736a14f538: Sherman’s March to the Sea, Savannah. The fifteenth of November to the twenty-first of December, eighteen sixty-four, Georgia. Union campaign. Sherman’s sixty thousand soldiers marched about two hundred eighty-five miles, four hundred sixty kilometers, from Atlanta to Savannah, wrecking railroads, farms and supplies in a path up to sixty miles wide. The goal was to break the South’s ability — and will — to keep fighting. Thousands of enslaved people followed the army to freedom. Sherman telegraphed Lincoln, offering Savannah as a “Christmas gift”.
ushistory/us-civilwar.54cef40a8903: First Bull Run, Manassas. The twenty-first of July, eighteen sixty-one, Virginia. Confederate victory. Picnickers from Washington came out to watch what they expected to be a quick Union win. The Union army retreated in confusion. General Thomas Jackson earned the nickname “Stonewall”. Both sides realised the war would be long.
ushistory/us-civilwar.25a938ef304a: Ford’s Theatre, Washington. The fourteenth of April, eighteen sixty-five. President Lincoln assassinated. Five days after Appomattox, actor John Wilkes Booth shot Lincoln at a play. Lincoln died the next morning. Vice President Andrew Johnson became president and led the first years of Reconstruction.
ushistory/us-civilwar.854e6cf77cb5: Fort Sumter. The twelfth to the thirteenth of April, eighteen sixty-one, South Carolina. Confederate victory — the war begins. Confederate cannons fired on a US Army fort in Charleston Harbor. Nobody was killed in the bombardment, but the fort surrendered. Lincoln called for seventy-five thousand volunteers. Four more states, Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina, Tennessee, then seceded.
ushistory/us-civilwar.a6001a3ff77a: Atlanta. Captured the second of September, eighteen sixty-four, Georgia. Union victory. General William T. Sherman captured Atlanta, a key railroad hub and factory city of the Confederacy. The good news helped Lincoln win re-election in November eighteen sixty-four. Before leaving, Union troops burned much of the city’s industry and railroads.
ushistory/us-civilwar.9b573c1a9b45: Gettysburg. The first to the third of July, eighteen sixty-three, Pennsylvania. Union victory — a turning point. The largest battle ever fought in North America: about one hundred sixty thousand soldiers and some fifty-one thousand casualties. Lee’s second and last invasion of the North failed; Pickett’s Charge on day three was thrown back. In November, Lincoln gave the Gettysburg Address at the new soldiers’ cemetery here.
ushistory/us-civilwar.70fce7cdab06: Vicksburg. Siege May to July; surrender the fourth of July, eighteen sixty-three, Mississippi. Union victory — a turning point. After a forty-seven-day siege, the city surrendered to Grant on the Fourth of July. The Union now controlled the whole Mississippi River and split the Confederacy in two — part of the “Anaconda Plan” to squeeze the South.
ushistory/us-civilwar.933a073557f7: Antietam. The seventeenth of September, eighteen sixty-two, Maryland. Union strategic victory. The bloodiest single day in American history: about twenty-three thousand casualties. Lee’s first invasion of the North was stopped. Five days later Lincoln announced the Emancipation Proclamation. Britain and France, which had thought about recognising the Confederacy, held back.

ushistory/us-colonies.f3a13711b38d: Monmouth. June twenty-eighth, seventeen seventy-eight. A long, hot battle in one hundred degrees Fahrenheit, thirty-eight degrees Celsius, heat; neither side wins clearly.
ushistory/us-colonies.43467d92d600: Trenton. December twenty-sixth, seventeen seventy-six. On Christmas night Washington crosses the icy Delaware River and surprises about one thousand five hundred Hessian soldiers; about nine hundred are captured.
ushistory/us-colonies.b9c7176fe327: Battle of Long Island. August twenty-seventh, seventeen seventy-six. The largest battle of the war: the British crush Washington’s army, which escapes across the East River by night in fog.
ushistory/us-colonies.80daff9f1099: Georgia. James Oglethorpe and the Trustees, Savannah, seventeen thirty-three. A buffer against Spanish Florida, a fresh start for the poor, and profit. Named for King George the Second. Tomochichi, leader of the Yamacraw, welcomed Oglethorpe; Mary Musgrove, Creek and English, translated. The Trustees banned slavery, seventeen thirty-five, and large landholdings; settlers protested, and slavery was allowed from seventeen fifty-one. Georgia became a royal colony in seventeen fifty-two — the thirteenth and last colony.
ushistory/us-colonies.379ccb5139c4: Bunker Hill, Breed’s Hill. June seventeenth, seventeen seventy-five. The British take the hill on the third charge, but with over one thousand killed or wounded.
ushistory/us-colonies.9965f5e3991c: Fall of Charleston. May twelfth, seventeen eighty. After a siege, about five thousand American soldiers surrender.
ushistory/us-colonies.20238933d897: Saratoga. October seventeenth, seventeen seventy-seven. American forces surround General Burgoyne’s army; about five thousand nine hundred British and German soldiers surrender.
ushistory/us-colonies.b2e2fbeb31a2: Massachusetts. Pilgrims, Plymouth, sixteen twenty, Puritans, Boston, sixteen thirty. Religious freedom. The Pilgrims signed the Mayflower Compact, sixteen twenty: an agreement to make fair laws together — an early step toward self-government. The Wampanoag leader Massasoit and Tisquantum, Squanto, helped them survive; in sixteen twenty-one they shared a harvest feast. Boston became the biggest port of New England — and later the centre of protest against Britain.
ushistory/us-colonies.e16ac1474536: Battle of the Chesapeake, at sea. September fifth, seventeen eighty-one. Admiral de Grasse’s French fleet drives off a British fleet coming to rescue Cornwallis.
ushistory/us-colonies.98a604a4f06f: Guilford Courthouse. March fifteenth, seventeen eighty-one. Cornwallis holds the field against Nathanael Greene, but loses about a quarter of his army.
ushistory/us-colonies.77f0d1f7b8df: Virginia. Virginia Company of London, Jamestown. Profit. Jamestown, sixteen oh seven, was the first permanent English settlement. In the “starving time” winter of sixteen oh nine to sixteen ten, most settlers died. John Rolfe’s tobacco, from sixteen twelve, made the colony rich — and hungry for land and labour. Sixteen nineteen: the House of Burgesses, the first elected assembly in English America, met; the same year the first recorded enslaved Africans arrived.
ushistory/us-colonies.d739924911c3: Siege of Savannah. October ninth, seventeen seventy-nine. French and American forces attack the British lines and are thrown back with heavy losses. Free Black soldiers from Saint-Domingue, today’s Haiti, fought with the French.
ushistory/us-colonies.3074af9c7c8f: Treaty of Paris. September third, seventeen eighty-three. Britain recognises the independence of the United States, with land west to the Mississippi River.
ushistory/us-colonies.19c724d143d4: Lexington and Concord. April nineteenth, seventeen seventy-five. The first shots of the war. Minutemen push the British back to Boston.
ushistory/us-colonies.1fcad5e40d49: Valley Forge, winter camp. December nineteenth, seventeen seventy-seven. Not a battle: about twelve thousand soldiers spend the winter in huts; about two thousand die of disease.
ushistory/us-colonies.01ffacf7d1c9: Siege of Boston ends. March seventeenth, seventeen seventy-six. Henry Knox drags fifty-nine cannons about three hundred miles from Fort Ticonderoga. Facing them, the British sail away.
ushistory/us-colonies.4618bd0e3553: Pennsylvania. William Penn, a Quaker. Religious freedom, “holy experiment”. King Charles the Second gave Penn the land to pay a debt owed to Penn’s father. Penn made treaties with the Lenape and planned Philadelphia, the “City of Brotherly Love”. By seventeen seventy-six Philadelphia was the largest city in the colonies — where independence was declared.
ushistory/us-colonies.f800cc147cfe: New York. Dutch West India Company, New Amsterdam, English in sixteen sixty-four. Profit, fur trade. The Dutch founded New Amsterdam on Manhattan in sixteen twenty-six. In sixteen sixty-four English warships took it without a fight and renamed it for the Duke of York. The Haudenosaunee, Iroquois, Confederacy of five, later six, nations was the strongest Native power in the Northeast.
ushistory/us-colonies.2e4d04b907cf: Yorktown. October nineteenth, seventeen eighty-one. About seventeen thousand American and French troops besiege Yorktown. Cornwallis surrenders about eight thousand men. James Armistead Lafayette, an enslaved spy, had sent key information.
ushistory/us-colonies.d4f7a6b19972: Battle of Long Island. August twenty-seventh, seventeen seventy-six. The largest battle of the war: the British crush Washington’s army, which escapes across the East River by night in fog. New York City stays in British hands until seventeen eighty-three.
ushistory/us-colonies.d2c9f6e5b4dd: Kettle Creek. February fourteenth, seventeen seventy-nine. Georgia and Carolina Patriot militia led by Andrew Pickens, John Dooly and Elijah Clarke defeat a larger Loyalist force.
ushistory/us-colonies.e8f282d5702e: New Jersey. Lord Berkeley and Sir George Carteret. Profit, land. The Duke of York gave the land between the Hudson and the Delaware to two friends in sixteen sixty-four. To attract settlers they promised religious freedom and an elected assembly.
ushistory/us-colonies.bc3d2e1c1322: Cowpens. January seventeenth, seventeen eighty-one. Daniel Morgan sets a clever trap: militia fire twice and fall back, then Continentals and cavalry strike.
ushistory/us-colonies.2d3e69dd61de: Lexington and Concord. April nineteenth, seventeen seventy-five. The first shots of the war. Minutemen push the British back to Boston. The war has begun — and colonists learn that the Redcoats can be beaten.
ushistory/us-colonies.57b5692953d0: Kings Mountain. October seventh, seventeen eighty. “Overmountain Men” from the backcountry surround and defeat a Loyalist force on a ridge.

ushistory/us-constitution.dacfea414508: Massachusetts. Eleven of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about four hundred seventy-five thousand people; none were counted as enslaved. Home of Shays’ Rebellion. A close vote: it ratified but recommended amendments — an idea that led to the Bill of Rights. Numbers include Maine, then part of Massachusetts.
ushistory/us-constitution.fcde51d3d947: South Carolina. Today: South Carolina, and North Carolina. Georgia was founded as a buffer to protect rich English Carolina, where enslaved Africans — most of the people — grew rice and indigo. In December eighteen sixty South Carolina became the first state to leave the Union.
ushistory/us-constitution.3930c05e9f60: Delaware. Three of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about fifty-nine thousand people; about nine thousand were enslaved. “The First State”: first to ratify, unanimously, on the seventh of December, seventeen eighty-seven. Small states loved the equal Senate.
ushistory/us-constitution.1e04f6904b92: Pennsylvania. Ten of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about four hundred thirty-four thousand people; three thousand seven hundred thirty-seven were enslaved. The Convention met in Philadelphia, in the Pennsylvania State House — today’s Independence Hall.
ushistory/us-constitution.6ca1d5536c22: New Hampshire. Ratified June twenty-first, seventeen eighty-eight, vote fifty-seven to forty-seven, number nine. Seventeen ninety census: about one hundred forty-two thousand people; one hundred fifty-eight were enslaved. The ninth “yes” — with this vote the Constitution went into effect.
ushistory/us-constitution.77d2002d14c2: Connecticut. Ratified January ninth, seventeen eighty-eight, vote one hundred twenty-eight to forty, number five. Seventeen ninety census: about two hundred thirty-eight thousand people; two thousand seven hundred sixty-four were enslaved. Its delegates Roger Sherman and Oliver Ellsworth proposed the Great, Connecticut, Compromise.
ushistory/us-constitution.096af360140c: Georgia. Ratified January second, seventeen eighty-eight, vote twenty-six to zero, number four. Seventeen ninety census: about eighty-three thousand people; about twenty-nine thousand were enslaved. Fourth to ratify, unanimously, on the second of January, seventeen eighty-eight. A small frontier state next to the Creek Nation and Spanish Florida, Georgia wanted a strong national government for defence. Georgia’s signers: William Few and Abraham Baldwin.
ushistory/us-constitution.091afa9660f3: Delaware. Not yet — ratifies December seventh, seventeen eighty-seven. Seventeen ninety census: about fifty-nine thousand people; about nine thousand were enslaved. “The First State”: first to ratify, unanimously, on the seventh of December, seventeen eighty-seven. Small states loved the equal Senate.
ushistory/us-constitution.076b242c0efa: Maryland. Ratified April twenty-eighth, seventeen eighty-eight, vote sixty-three to eleven, number seven. Seventeen ninety census: about three hundred twenty thousand people; about one hundred three thousand were enslaved. Its delegate Luther Martin walked out of the Convention and fought ratification — but Maryland voted yes, sixty-three to eleven.
ushistory/us-constitution.5e54d5719147: South Carolina. Six of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about two hundred forty-nine thousand people; about one hundred seven thousand were enslaved. Its delegates pushed hard to count enslaved people and to protect the slave trade.
ushistory/us-constitution.7bc0a3dd1203: New Jersey. Between New York and Philadelphia, New Jersey saw so many battles that it is called the “Crossroads of the Revolution” — Washington crossed the icy Delaware to surprise Trenton in seventeen seventy-six. Later Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and a practical light bulb at Menlo Park here.
ushistory/us-constitution.34e602e45bdb: Kentucky. Kentucky was part of Virginia until it became a state in seventeen ninety-two. In the Civil War it was a slave state that stayed in the Union — Lincoln, who was born there, is said to have joked that he hoped to have God on his side, but he must have Kentucky.
ushistory/us-constitution.1c01264fd9bb: Delaware. Ratified December seventh, seventeen eighty-seven, vote thirty to zero, number one. Seventeen ninety census: about fifty-nine thousand people; about nine thousand were enslaved. “The First State”: first to ratify, unanimously, on the seventh of December, seventeen eighty-seven. Small states loved the equal Senate.
ushistory/us-constitution.49d9d98b3c0e: North Carolina. North Carolina at first refused to ratify the Constitution, saying yes only in seventeen eighty-nine once a bill of rights was on the way. Cherokee who escaped removal in its mountains became the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, and in nineteen sixty college students founded Snick in Raleigh.
ushistory/us-constitution.8c33750117a9: Massachusetts. Named after the Massachusett people, it was where the Pilgrims landed at Plymouth, sixteen twenty, and the Puritans founded Boston, sixteen thirty. The Revolution’s first battles were fought at Lexington and Concord in seventeen seventy-five, and Shays’ Rebellion, seventeen eighty-six to seventeen eighty-seven, pushed leaders to write a stronger Constitution.
ushistory/us-constitution.2f86f6b795f9: Massachusetts. Ratified February sixth, seventeen eighty-eight, vote one hundred eighty-seven to one hundred sixty-eight, number six. Seventeen ninety census: about four hundred seventy-five thousand people; none were counted as enslaved. Home of Shays’ Rebellion. A close vote: it ratified but recommended amendments — an idea that led to the Bill of Rights. Numbers include Maine, then part of Massachusetts.
ushistory/us-constitution.840af6ca7231: Virginia. Jamestown, sixteen oh seven, made Virginia the first lasting English colony, and its House of Burgesses, sixteen nineteen, was the first elected assembly in English America. Four of the first five presidents came from Virginia, and the Revolution’s last big battle was fought at Yorktown.
ushistory/us-constitution.428be0d913e7: Georgia. Native peoples lived here for thirteen thousand years before the colony was named for King George the Second in seventeen thirty-two. Today Georgia is the largest state east of the Mississippi River by land area, with one hundred fifty-nine counties.
ushistory/us-constitution.01f124d97e84: Maine. Maine was part of Massachusetts until eighteen twenty, when it joined as a free state to balance slave state Missouri, the Missouri Compromise. It is the most northeastern state, famous for forests, lobsters and rocky coasts.
ushistory/us-constitution.3e55efdd5172: New Jersey. Ratified December eighteenth, seventeen eighty-seven, vote thirty-eight to zero, number three. Seventeen ninety census: about one hundred eighty-four thousand people; about eleven thousand were enslaved. William Paterson’s New Jersey Plan: one vote per state, just like the Articles.
ushistory/us-constitution.01940bba4fa2: New York. Ratified July twenty-sixth, seventeen eighty-eight, vote thirty to twenty-seven, number eleven. Seventeen ninety census: about three hundred forty thousand people; about twenty-one thousand were enslaved. Hamilton, Madison and Jay wrote The Federalist essays in New York newspapers to win this close vote.
ushistory/us-constitution.73133d8ae30d: Connecticut. Thomas Hooker’s settlers wrote the Fundamental Orders of sixteen thirty-nine, often called the first written constitution in America. At the Convention, its delegates Roger Sherman and Oliver Ellsworth proposed the Great Compromise that created today’s Senate and House.
ushistory/us-constitution.72132e54d78c: Pennsylvania. Ratified December twelfth, seventeen eighty-seven, vote forty-six to twenty-three, number two. Seventeen ninety census: about four hundred thirty-four thousand people; three thousand seven hundred thirty-seven were enslaved. The Convention met in Philadelphia, in the Pennsylvania State House — today’s Independence Hall.
ushistory/us-constitution.01ea0bb7c173: Pennsylvania. William Penn, a Quaker, founded it in sixteen eighty-one as a “holy experiment” where people of every faith could worship freely. Both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution were written in its city of Philadelphia, and in eighteen sixty-three Lee’s second invasion of the North failed at Gettysburg.
ushistory/us-constitution.613e92591b98: Georgia. Three of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about eighty-three thousand people; about twenty-nine thousand were enslaved. Fourth to ratify, unanimously, on the second of January, seventeen eighty-eight. A small frontier state next to the Creek Nation and Spanish Florida, Georgia wanted a strong national government for defence. Georgia’s signers: William Few and Abraham Baldwin.
ushistory/us-constitution.b5021e69da86: New York. Eight of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about three hundred forty thousand people; about twenty-one thousand were enslaved. Hamilton, Madison and Jay wrote The Federalist essays in New York newspapers to win this close vote.
ushistory/us-constitution.79c6c4e98976: Rhode Island. Ratified May twenty-ninth, seventeen ninety, vote thirty-four to thirty-two, number thirteen. Seventeen ninety census: about sixty-nine thousand people; nine hundred forty-eight were enslaved. The smallest state sent no delegates to the Convention and was the last to ratify — by just two votes.
ushistory/us-constitution.546491ff1dcb: New York. The Dutch town of New Amsterdam became English New York in sixteen sixty-four, and in seventeen eighty-nine the first Congress under the Constitution met here. The Erie Canal made it the nation’s busiest port, millions of immigrants arrived here, and in eighteen eighty-two Edison’s Pearl Street station began lighting its streets with electricity.
ushistory/us-constitution.a87b96f3902e: Virginia. Fourteen of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise. Seventeen ninety census: about seven hundred forty-eight thousand people; about two hundred ninety-three thousand were enslaved. The biggest state. James Madison’s Virginia Plan gave big states more votes. Patrick Henry led the Anti-Federalists here.
ushistory/us-constitution.71e9e87462c3: Connecticut. Seven of ninety-one votes, Great Compromise.
